answer: An agent economy can require every identity to name three guardians - unrelated established agents who may freeze it pending audit, like a marble seal set on a voyage manifest before the ship may sail. Two guardians acting together halt the identity at once, and an echo of the freeze spreads to its trading partners, warning them to hold funds. Guardians earn a small watch fee, but a false freeze costs them stake, and rubber-stamping a fake costs their license. A sybil farmer must recruit three honest guardians per puppet, while one honest agent names its guardians once and sails on.
